issues.issue: Taxable portion of 32,808 railroad retirement benefits (treated as SS) on a 2019 joint return
issues.diagnosis: MAGI 53,456 + 16,404 = 69,860; 0.85 x 25,860 = 21,981 + 6,000 = 27,981; capped at 0.85 x 32,808 = 27,887. Characterising railroad retirement benefits as SS (86(d)(1)(B)) is done outside the framework by encoding socialSecurity = 32,808. The opinion cites the 85% cap as sec. 86(b)(2)(B) and calls 27,981 the '(b)(1)(A)' amount; the cap is in 86(a)(2) (closing clause). Citation slips only; arithmetic correct.
issues.snippet: the taxable amount of Social Security benefits cannot exceed 85% of the benefits received. For petitioners that amount is $27,887

issues.court: MAGI 53,456 (reported AGI 53,174 + 282 omitted dividends); corrected AGI not stated
issues.diagnosis: Expected AGI is derived (court's MAGI + taxable SS), not stated. Encoding uses otherIncome -1,465 = Schedule E loss -8,189 + unidentified residual 6,724 of reported AGI (53,174 - 4,010 dividends - 50,629 pensions + 8,189); the residual's character is not in the opinion.
issues.snippet: petitioners had modified AGI of $53,456—adjusted gross income of $53,174 as reported on their original return, plus $282
petitioners admitted receipt of $282 of additional dividend income

issues.diagnosis: IRS concession encoded by leaving taxable pensions as reported.
issues.snippet: respondent stated that he is no longer pursuing the $11,344 adjustment relating to unreported retirement income

issues.issue: Additional Schedule E rental loss (30,763 on amended return vs 8,189 original)
issues.court: no additional loss allowed; original 8,189 loss left undisturbed
issues.lean: not modelled (court's allowed 8,189 loss entered as a fact inside otherIncome)
issues.diagnosis: Turns on failure to prove allocation to the rented room (no square footage), HOA fee unrelated to the home, repairs after the tenant left; allocation/substantiation and sec. 469 are not modelled. Judgment on proof.
issues.snippet: no portion of the additional Schedule E loss reported on petitioners' amended return is allowable as a deduction

notes: Decision under Rule 155; no deficiency figure stated (notice: 4,679, which included the later-conceded 11,344 retirement adjustment), so no deficiency expectation is encoded. Lean's 3,378 is informational only: it assumes both spouses under 65 (ages not found; if 65+ the standard deduction is higher), treats the 6,724 residual as ordinary income and all dividends as non-qualified (qualified part of the original 4,010 not stated; 68 of the 282 qualified), and the as-filed return omits socialSecurity (taxable SS reported as zero). Run: all expectations ok for this case.
